output.methodChoice: D (competing hypotheses) with C's verify-before-acting logic: several rival causes, and the key question is whether the rise is real.
output.brief: The rise at store 14 may not be real. The Q1–Q3 figures are estimates from partial cycle counts, with an error band of about ±0.6 points a quarter. In past years, about half of two-quarter rises like this one were not confirmed by the year-end full count. Store 14's own full-count shrink was 1.5–1.8% in FY2023–25. The incident log is also unreliable as a trend signal: a chain-wide app launched on 1 April, and recorded incidents rose chain-wide while shrink stayed flat. Neighbouring stores 9 and 22 show no common pattern. Department sales mix barely moved, so a mix shift doesn't explain it. The self-checkout lanes, customer theft and staff theft all remain possible, and none is established. The ethics-line tip was checked on CCTV and showed bale runs, not theft. What to do: keep store 14 in the 7 December full count and reject the proposal to drop it. That count is the cheapest way to find out whether the loss is real. Don't spend on a guard, pull the lanes, or suspend the stocker until the count is compared with the interim figures. If the loss is confirmed, run a targeted review by department and item type. I'm moderately sure of this, and the main gap is that I haven't seen item-level or receiving data.
